Days are 6 focused hours of the owner's time, branch cut to merge-ready, excluding the wait for Dave's merge.

method_notes.bottom-up: Bottom-up. For each unit I listed the tasks its scope implies (tables and migrations, functions, Server Actions, pages, stories, unit, database and e2e tests) and sized each one. I then added review and fix-round time: about 0.25 to 0.5 day of pipeline overhead on a standard fan-out unit and about 0.5 to 1 day on a critical one, which covers the swarm, the race and access tests, and Dave's diff read. The anchors are real-world: about 2 to 3 solo days for a Better Auth magic-link setup with roles; 2 to 4 days for a wide Drizzle schema with Zod and DAL tests; 3 to 4 days for eight Storybook primitives with the a11y addon; 3 to 5 days for a SKIP LOCKED outbox with concurrency tests. The agent speed-up is largest on breadth units (schemas, templates, admin CRUD, copy, Code Connect) and smallest on locking and money units, where race tests and review rounds take most of the time. Data issue: the task list names U-076, but the record has U-076a, U-076b and U-076c, and no U-076. I estimated all three and added a U-076 row that is their sum. Use the three and drop U-076, or the editorial admin is counted twice. Where the plan may be systematically wrong: (1) The money cluster is about 20 critical units (confirmOrder branches, refunds, gifts, release and reconciliation). They share contracts that keep moving as each lands, so rework will land on already-merged units, and no single unit's estimate shows it. Expect the sum of p to be more realistic there than the PERT mean. (2) U-021a, U-100 and U-104 surface fixes in other units, and those fixes are not in any estimate. (3) Some U2 scores rest on young-stack unknowns (Cache Components, Better Auth step-up, React Aria bottom sheet). Those unknowns hit the first unit that meets them and are cheap afterwards, so later sibling units may come in under estimate. The Figma variables REST API is Enterprise-only, which may make U-023's export a manual plugin step.
method_notes.analogy: Each unit was scaled from its nearest analogue. For checkout, booking-widget, confirmation and failure-state units, the analogue is Dave's prior client checkout: about 65 PRs in roughly 50 working days, with place-order taking three passes. For backend units it is typical industry work, for example a Better Auth magic-link setup at 2-4 days solo, a transactional outbox at 3-5 days solo, and eight Storybook primitives at about a week solo. Routed estimates assume roughly 0.5 days of pipeline overhead per unit (reviews, CI, a fix round), plus about 0.5 days more on the critical tier for review-swarm and Dave's diff read. That overhead is why agent units save less than 2x against solo: routed m sums to about 228 days (222 without U-046) and solo m to about 371. The task list names U-076, but units.yaml splits it into U-076a, U-076b and U-076c, so the U-076 row covers all three. Done spikes U-013 and U-028 are excluded. The analogue suggests the per-unit sums are systematically optimistic. The prior project ran six weeks over a window of about four to five weeks. Its overrun came from rework across units (the place-order passes), and this breakdown hides that kind of rework in typed stubs and moving contracts: confirmOrder branches U-062a, U-064a and U-065a, the contract between U-079b and U-081, the U-066b reinstatement hook, and the 'whichever lands second' axe-matrix rows. So I would put a project-level 1.3-1.5x integration factor on top of the PERT path rather than pad individual units.
method_notes.pipeline: I anchored on pipeline elapsed time per tier: a C1 U1 standard fan-out unit is about half a day (an hour of agent build, review, one small fix round, CI), C2 units 1 to 2 days, and C3 money or lock units 2.5 to 4 days. Critical tier adds about half a day to a day for /review-swarm, the in-diff race or access tests, and Dave's diff read. Tails come from what costs time in practice: flaky real-database and Playwright tests (U-014a, U-052, U-064a, U-105), rebases over hot shared files (confirmOrder, reserveSpaces, browse and home card queries, migrations, seeds), and scope manifests that are very long (U-047a, U-049, U-055, U-114). Solo estimates are hands-on time for one strong engineer, usually 1.5 to 2 times routed: agents compress typing and test-writing, but much less so for review, debugging and judgment on money paths. Note that units.yaml has no U-076: it has U-076a, U-076b and U-076c. I estimated U-076 as the three combined (routed m about 1.5 + 1.5 + 1.5, slightly discounted for shared context), and the PM should split it back out. I think the plan is systematically optimistic in two ways. First, it treats each unit's rebase and fix rounds on hot files as independent, but money units that land close together on confirmOrder and reserveSpaces will collide. Second, host and ops screens have no drawn design, so review rounds on UI there are likely to go past m.
method_notes.risk: I set a base per route and score (fan-out C1U1 about 0.25/0.5/1, C2 standard about 0.5/1/2.5, C2 critical about 0.75/1.5/3 to 4, C3 critical money paths about 1/2 to 2.5/5 to 6, Dave-led C3 pattern-setters about 1.5 to 2/3/6 to 8). Then I moved each unit using the 03-scores rationales and the spikes: U-008a, U-009 and U-078 keep a tail for the stale build-time page the spike saw after updateTag, and the money paths keep a tail for race tests that pass in isolation but flake against real Postgres in CI. Solo runs about 1.5 to 2 times the fan-out route. On human-led units the gap is smaller (about 1.3 times), because there Dave already does most of the work. The requested list names U-076, but units.yaml splits it into U-076a, U-076b and U-076c, so my U-076 row covers all three (most likely about 1.5 + 1 + 1). It should be split or replaced before critical-path.ts reads it. Where I think the plan is systematically wrong: per-unit estimates miss the cost at the seams. confirmOrder's typed stubs, U-056's refund contract and the gift branches will each send rework back into units that already merged. About 35 units each add rows to the U-100 axe matrix, and the late launch units (U-099, U-100, U-104, U-096) will surface fixes that get charged to no unit. So the sum of the per-unit m values probably understates the total by 10 to 20%, even if each p is honest.
